newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to give banks new capital rules from 1999.
newsitem.headline: Russia to give banks new capital rules from 1999.

text.p: Russia has set a minimum requirement for bank capital at one million European Currency Units (ECUs) from 1999 and will limit activities of those with capital below five million, the central bank said on Friday.
Those banks with capital below one million Ecu by January 1, 1999 will be deprived of their banking status and will have to be re-organised or liquidated, the bank said in a statement.

Banks with a capital below five million Ecu will be confined to limited domestic activities. They will not be able to own more than 25 percent of any other financial organisation and will not be able to trade gold.
Last year, the central bank set the minimum capital of a new bank at two million Ecu, to be raised gradually to five million by July 1 1998. But there are still hundreds of banks with low capital.
Charter capital requirements were last raised to 12 billion roubles from six billion roubles in May last year. ($1=5,676 roubles)
